entry.title: Clarify when the "labels" attribute of <input> is null
entry.content:
Description

The current text says that HTMLInputElement.labels is a NodeList, "if the element is not hidden", which is ambiguous, because it can be an element with the global "hidden" attribute or an input whose "type" is "hidden".

HTMLInputElement.labels is a NodeList when the global "hidden" attribute is set on the element.

Motivation

To fix an error.

Additional details

the labels IDL attribute of input elements, on getting, must return that NodeList object, and that same value must always be returned, unless this element is an input element whose type attribute is in the Hidden state, in which case it must instead return null.

https://html.spec.whatwg.org/multipage/forms.html#dom-lfe-labels

Related issues and pull requests

entry.title: WebGL best practices: fix VRAM budget advice and update canvas sizing guidance
entry.content:
Description

This updates the parts of the WebGL best practices page that were called out in #26597:

  • Estimate a per-pixel VRAM budget: the three steps were written inline as "1) … 2) … 3)", so I turned them into a proper list. I also removed the line saying mobile devices usually have smaller screens. In device pixels that's no longer true, since a lot of phones have as many pixels as a laptop or desktop display, or more.
  • Memory usage of depth and stencil formats: added a short note on why this matters in practice. It feeds into your VRAM estimate, and it means a combined depth-stencil attachment usually costs no more than a 24-bit depth-only one.
  • devicePixelRatio and high-dpi rendering: now points to ResizeObserver with device-pixel-content-box as the main approach. Pre-snapping stays as a fallback, with a note that it doesn't work when the canvas is sized by its container.
  • ResizeObserver and 'device-pixel-content-box': replaced the promise-based getDevicePixelSize() example with the more common pattern of setting the canvas size inside the observer callback. It falls back to contentBoxSize * devicePixelRatio when devicePixelContentBoxSize isn't available (Safari doesn't support it yet). It also handles browsers that throw on the unknown box option.

Motivation

Some of the advice was outdated or didn't hold up. The old example also made an app wait on a promise before it knew the canvas size, which isn't how most WebGL apps handle resizing.

Additional details

  • I ran the new example in Chromium at a device pixel ratio of 1.5. A canvas with a 353.9 × 233.7 CSS box got a 531 × 351 drawing buffer, matching its device-pixel size. I also forced the fallback path (no devicePixelContentBoxSize, and observe() throwing for the box option), and it still sized the canvas correctly.
  • Support info for devicePixelContentBoxSize comes from BCD.
  • I left the "Use texStorage to create textures" section alone. The issue says texSubImage2D uploads are slower than texImage2D in Chrome, but I couldn't confirm that's still the case, so I'd rather leave that one to someone who knows.
  • markdownlint, Prettier, cspell and the front-matter linter pass. A local rari build of the page reports no flaws, and the new in-page links resolve.

Related issues and pull requests

Relates to #26597 (covers everything in it except the texStorage point)

entry.title: fix(api): remove outdated Firefox beforeunload bfcache claims
entry.content:
Description

This PR removes the claim that Firefox won't put pages with beforeunload listeners in the bfcache, along with the same claim on the sendBeacon() and pagehide pages.

Motivation

  • The beforeunload usage notes said Firefox excludes pages with beforeunload listeners from the bfcache. Firefox has allowed these pages in the bfcache since version 116, so I removed the bullet. That left a one-item list, so I turned it into a paragraph. I also removed the sentence saying that listening sparingly minimizes the effect on performance, since the removed bullet was the only reason given for it.
  • The "Legacy events" section of the sendBeacon() page had a separate line saying Firefox excludes pages with beforeunload handlers, which I removed. The comparison with pagehide now only mentions unload.
  • The pagehide page said pagehide is compatible with the bfcache "unlike the unload and beforeunload events". It now only mentions unload.

Additional details

  • Firefox bugs: 1837045 (enabled in release, Firefox 116) and 1741671 (enabled in Nightly).
  • The docshell.shistory.bfcache.ship_allow_beforeunload_listeners pref now defaults to true on all platforms in Firefox's current source.
  • markdownlint-cli2 and prettier --check report 0 issues on the changed files, and the front-matter linter passes.

entry.title: Consolidate Tools and setup Learn section content
entry.content:
Description

As per mdn/mdn#822, the Tools and setup section of the learning area is outdated and repeats content available elsewhere on MDN. It is also a maintenance burden — quite a few parts of it would be better updated so they point to the tool manufacturer's docs rather than us repeating it.

This PR updates the Tools and setup section to fix this problem. The following list provides notes on what I've done for each article in the section:

  • What software do I need to build a website?: This stuff is covered in Installing basic software, so I've removed it and redirected to there.
  • How much does it cost to do something on the web?: Some of this stuff was useful; I've put those bits in Publishing your website and deleted it and redirected to there. I also restructured the "Publishing your website" guide and updated the gh pages info there, pointing to GitHub's docs where appropriate and adding guidance in between. It's a shame there isn't one simple GitHub guide to follow to easily get something on gh-pages.
  • What text editors are available?: Covered in Installing basic software. Deleted and redirected to there.
  • What are browser developer tools?: This is still genuinely useful. I've copyedited it to improve the text and bring a few things up to date, and crunched the images a bit to reduce file size.
  • How do you make sure your website works properly?: This is a bit of a strange mishmash of debugging tips. The bit about the network inspector and HTTP statuses was quite useful and not covered anywhere else, so I've added a brief network inspector section that covers it to What are browser developer tools?, then deleted it and redirected to there.
  • How do you set up a local testing server?: This is genuinely useful and linked to in a few places. I've given it a copy edit and improved a few things.
  • How do you upload files to a web server?: Another article that covers publishing web content. Again, consolidated, deleted, and redirected to Publishing your website
  • How do I use GitHub Pages?: It is not worth us maintaining a separate page on github pages. I've deleted this and redirected to the Version control module page. I've made sure that page includes a prominent link to the gh pages step by step on "Publishing your website".
  • How do you host your website on Google App Engine?: This was already deleted and redirected to the Google App Engine docs, so I've just removed the link from the section landing page.
  • What tools are available to debug and improve website performance?: already removed and redirected to the relevant dev tools documentation, so I've just removed the link from the landing page.

There are only two articles left in the "Tools and setup" section now, so maybe a future PR could look at restructuring further.

Motivation

entry.title: Document sanitization during HTML parsing
entry.content:
Description

Update the HTML Sanitizer API overview and all six Element, ShadowRoot, and Document method references to describe sanitization during parsing rather than a separate pass over the completed DOM. Explain the observable consequences for adjacent text nodes, custom element construction, resource-fetching side effects, and declarative shadow roots, with a focused example showing a replaced <b> producing one text node.

Also correct the default-sanitizer example to pass { sanitizer: "default" } to setHTMLUnsafe(), fix its inconsistent variable names and whitespace output, and clarify fragment parsing's top-level shadow-template behavior.

Motivation

The HTML Standard changed in whatwg/html#12756. The existing descriptions still teach the earlier parse-then-sanitize model and the unsafe example currently omits the sanitizer it claims to use. This documents the current specification and notes that some browsers still sanitize after parsing, producing different DOM structures.

Additional details

  • Specification: whatwg/html#12756 (merged).
  • Associated web-platform tests: web-platform-tests/wpt#62492, including custom element construction and declarative shadow-root cases.
  • Addresses the review at #46132 (comment).
  • Validation: Markdown lint, front-matter lint, Prettier, CSpell, and git diff --check passed for the changed content.
  • Built all seven changed pages with Rari: no issues reported. After the separate source/diff review and wording refinements, rebuilt all seven pages and checked formatting again: no issues reported.

Related issues and pull requests

Fixes #46132.

Related to #46148 (the release-note task); this PR updates the overview and API references.

entry.title: Document conditional create
entry.content:
Fixes #42516.

The main questions I have are:

1. What exactly the conditions are for conditional mediation. The spec is quite opaque here:

For create(), if a user has previously consented to credential creation and the user agent knows it recently mediated an authentication, then the create() call may resolve without additional prominent modal interaction. If the user agent did not recently mediate an authentication or does not have consent for credential creation, then the call must throw a "NotAllowedError" DOMException.

(https://w3c.github.io/webappsec-credential-management/#mediation-requirements).

I've glossed this based on Ricky Mondello's talk (http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=otObbUSxcqs&t=10m50s) and the web.dev guide (https://developer.chrome.com/docs/identity/webauthn-conditional-create#how_it_works)

2. What the mediation option to create() means for other credential types, such as passwords. AFAICS the spec says nothing here. Testing suggests that it is just ignored.

3. What mediation values other than conditional mean for public key credentials. Again AFAICS they are just ignored, so I've opted not to list them even though they are in the IDL.

Also, I think we should take all this stuff out and into a separate guide page, but in a follow-up, please.

entry.title: Clarify user-defined nature of `<dashed-ident>`s
entry.content:
Description

This PR contains a 1 line copy change that hopefully clarifies an ambiguity in the <dashed-ident> docs around their user-defined nature.

Motivation

I was a little confused when I read the second clause here:

However, some `<custom-ident>`s are defined by the CSS language itself; `<dashed-ident>`s will never be defined in CSS.

The second clause is echoing the previous clause that mentions the CSS language, but I didn't interpret it that way at first. in CSS feels a bit too generic to me: is it referring to the CSS language, or CSS in general, the latter of which would include user-authored CSS.

I feel like contrasting against the first clause by stating that dashed idents will always be defined by the user helps highlight the difference and avoids this confusion.

That being said, maybe it was worded this way for a nuanced reason that I'm not aware of, so please provide feedback if that's the case.

    • network.continueRequest

Spec links

  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-addIntercept
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-continueRequest
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-failRequest
  • https://w3c.github.io/webdriver-bidi/#command-network-removeIntercept

Related issue

Doc issue: mdn/mdn#851

Compat quirks worth looking into:

  • Compat data for the continueRequest parameters in Firefox. All three come from my test run:
    • url: for a fetch(), the rewritten request reaches the new URL and the events report a 200 from it, but the page's fetch() rejects with AbortError: The operation was aborted. A navigation with a rewritten URL works. BCD shows Firefox's url parameter as supported since 133. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
    • headers: Firefox sends only the headers in the list, so a list without Host produces a request with no Host header (my server answered 400). Chrome still sends Host, Cookie, User-Agent and its other network headers. BCD shows Firefox's headers parameter as supported. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
    • body: with a longer body for a POST request, Firefox keeps the original Content-Length, so the server receives a truncated body. Chrome sends the new length. BCD shows Firefox's body parameter as supported. cc @whimboo for the compat sheet update.
